correctness.rationale: Exact Kraus/binomial thinning proves W_out(0)=(2/pi) sum_j p_j(1-2 eta)^j even for coherent density matrices. For eta>1/2 the initial nonnegative parity condition bounds odd population by 1/2, and coefficient monotonicity yields W_out >= (r^(2m)-r)/pi, attained if and only if p_1=p_2m=1/2. Strict convexity gives unique r=(2m)^(-1/(2m-1)); equality, cutoff plateaus, strict decreases and limiting value follow analytically. A standalone Kraus implementation corroborated this formula in 5600 random tests. No finite calculation is treated as a proof of universality.

originality.rationale: The assessed single theorem optimizes an origin-parity value under a simultaneous photon-cutoff and initial-parity constraint, includes exact attaining states/transmission, and resolves every finite cutoff. The 2021 review addresses distinct tasks. Abstract-only comparison for a 2013 Gaussian-adaptation study remains a residual priority risk, not an assertion of whole-document noncoverage.

value.rationale: The origin Wigner value is a directly measurable photon-parity functional. The natural finite-photon-resource and initially nonnegative-origin constraints ask how strongly ordinary loss can expose preexisting off-origin phase-space negativity at the origin. The theorem gives the exact all-state/all-loss floor, complete attaining input families, nontrivial adjacent-cutoff plateaus and a strict asymptotic staircase. It is not merely a table entry, and it explicitly avoids claiming that Gaussian loss creates global Wigner negativity.
